facts.statement: The type locality of Alanqa is Aferdou N'Chaft, located about 10 km northeast of Taouz near the village of Begaa.
facts.quote: The type locality of Alanqa is Aferdou N'Chaft, near the village of Begaa and approximately 10 km northeast of Taouz.

facts.statement: Paleontologists excavated sites in the Kem Kem Beds in April and November to December 2008.
facts.quote: a team of paleontologists conducted excavations at several sites in the Kem Kem Beds in April and November to December 2008

facts.statement: The jaws of Alanqa were straight and pointed, similar to those of Quetzalcoatlus and Zhejiangopterus.
facts.quote: The jaws were straight and pointed, like those of the azhdarchids Quetzalcoatlus and Zhejiangopterus.

facts.statement: A rostrum fragment described in 2015 was referred to Alanqa based on its origin.
facts.quote: A rostrum fragment was described in 2015 and referred to cf. Alanqa based on provenance.

facts.statement: Bony protuberances on the jaw suggest unusual functional specializations, possibly for visual display, soft tissue anchoring, or crushing hard-shelled food.
facts.quote: These imply an unusual functional specialization in this pterosaur; possible functions include visual display, anchoring of soft tissue, and crushing hard-shelled food.

facts.statement: Alanqa was likely prey for large predators including Spinosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus, Sauroniops, Aegisuchus, and possibly an unidentified madtsoiid snake.
facts.quote: Alanqa would be a prey item for the large predators of the ecosystem, such as theropod dinosaurs (Spinosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus, and Sauroniops), crocodyliforms like Aegisuchus, and possibly a currently-unidentified madtsoiid snake.

facts.statement: Alanqa lived during the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage) in what is now southeastern Morocco.
facts.quote: Alanqa is a genus of alanqid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous period (Cenomanian stage) of what is now the Kem Kem Group of southeastern Morocco.

facts.statement: Alanqa inhabited a freshwater delta system during the late Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Alanqa inhabited the late Cenomanian Kem Kem Group, which represented a freshwater delta system.

facts.statement: Alanqa was initially classified in the Azhdarchidae based on jaw similarities to Quetzalcoatlus and Zhejiangopterus.
facts.quote: In its initial description, Alanqa was referred to the Azhdarchidae, based on the similarity of its jaws to those of Quetzalcoatlus and Zhejiangopterus.

facts.statement: A 2018 analysis suggested Alanqa was a thalassodromid, but this classification is not well-supported.
facts.quote: Another analysis, this time by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues in 2018, recovered Alanqa as a thalassodromid, sister taxon to Aerotitan (a pterosaur also assigned as an azhdarchid). However, this concept is not well-supported.

facts.statement: A 2022 study recovered Alanqa as a basal azhdarchoid related to Keresdrakon, forming the new clade Alanqidae.
facts.quote: A 2022 study by Rubi Pêgas and colleagues showed dissimilarities between Aerotitan and Alanqa, as well as other thalassodromines. The former was recovered as an azhdarchid, while Alanqa was recovered as a basal azhdarchoid related to Keresdrakon, both forming the new clade Alanqidae.

facts.statement: The name Alanqa comes from the Arabic word al-'anqā', referring to a mythical bird similar to the Persian Simurgh.
facts.quote: El nombre Alanqa viene de la palabra árabe العنقاء al-‘anqā’, para un fénix similar al Simurgh de la mitología persa.

facts.statement: Alanqa lived about 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian in southeastern Morocco.
facts.quote: Alanqa es la única especie del género de pterosaurio azdárquido que vivió a principios del período Cretácico Superior, hace 95 millones de años, durante el Cenomaniano en el sureste de Marruecos

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with related species, individuals known from jaw specimens probably had wingspans of about 4 meters.
facts.quote: Basándose en la comparación con especies relacionadas, los individuos conocidos de especímenes de la mandíbula de Alanqa saharica probablemente tenían envergaduras de cerca de 4 metros.

facts.statement: According to Ibrahim and colleagues, a vertebra likely from the same species suggests an individual with a wingspan of about 6 meters.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, de acuerdo con Ibrahim y colegas, la vértebra (la cual probablemente pertenece a la misma especie) parece venir de un individuo mayor, que mediría cerca de 6 metros de envergadura.

facts.statement: Two jaw fragments were described but not named by Wellnhofer and Buffetaut in 1999.
facts.quote: Dos de estos fragmentos fueron descritos anteriormente, sin dárseles un nombre, por Wellnhofer y Buffetaut en 1999.

facts.statement: Paleontologists excavated Kem Kem Beds sites with local villagers' assistance in April and November to December 2008.
facts.quote: Ayudados por pobladores locales, un equipo de paleontólogos había estado excavando en varias locaciones en los lechos de Kem Kem durante abril, y de noviembre a diciembre de 2008

facts.statement: Alanqa lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Alanqa is known only from five fragments of the front upper and lower jaws and possibly a neck vertebra.
rejected.quote: Alanqa is known only from five fragments of the front upper and lower jaws, and possibly a neck vertebra
